newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds, futures continue tracking U.S. debt.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds, futures continue tracking U.S. debt.

text.p: With little relevant news or data to influence the direction of German Bunds and futures on Tuesday the German market mirrored moves in U.S. Treasuries.
Dealers said they saw no independent impulse in relatively listless trade as bond markets continued to consolidate after heavy losses late last week.
March Bund futures were down nine basis points at 100.70, pulled lower after U.S. Treasuries started lower.
In the morning, the March contract had reached up above 101.00 points, but could not break through the resistance level decisively, although it briefly touched 101.05.
"The market generally wants to go sideways," said one dealer, "After the recovery on Monday everybody would be happy if we could just hold onto these levels until the end of the year."

Dealers said there was some reluctance for players to take fresh positions ahead of the year-end, which could keep a lid on any gains. They said the fact that Monday's rally had occured in relatively thin volumes was also a negative sign.
The March future traded in a range between 100.61 and 101.05 points. The 10-year Bund was at 103.27 by 1529 GMT, yielding 5.78 percent.
Chartists said the futures contract was well-supported at 100.61 and 100.49.

Pan-German consumer price data released in the morning showed a fall November to 1.4 percent year-on-year from 1.5 percent, which was a move in the right direction for the market, but no great surprise.
Focus is likely to shift back to the U.S. market later in the week, with November producer price data due on Wednesday and consumer prices on Thursday.
